prompts.notes.summary.detailed: Summarise the material for [purpose]. Length: [length]. Keep the main idea, key facts, the author's conclusions and the order of presentation. Add nothing of your own and don't evaluate. Copy any numbers exactly. Material: [text]
prompts.notes.summary.refine: For each point, add where in the text it's mentioned.
prompts.notes.summary.check: Here's my summary: [my version]. What important points did I miss?
prompts.notes.theses.short: List the main points of the text: [text]
prompts.notes.theses.detailed: List the main points of the material: 5–8 items, each a single claim by the author. After each, in brackets, give a short supporting quote from the text (up to 10 words). Separately mark which points the author argues for and which are just stated. Material: [text]
prompts.notes.theses.refine: Group the points by meaning and give each group a heading.
prompts.notes.theses.check: Which point could be challenged? Suggest a question I could ask the author.
prompts.notes.glossary.short: Make a glossary of terms from this material: [text]
prompts.notes.glossary.detailed: Make a glossary from the material. Table: term, definition as used in the text, an example or explanation, a related term. Sort alphabetically. If the text doesn't define a term, write “not defined in the text” and give the standard meaning. Material: [text]
prompts.notes.glossary.refine: Keep only the 10 terms you can't understand the material without.
prompts.notes.glossary.check: Quiz me: give a definition and I'll name the term.
prompts.notes.questions.short: Turn my notes into 10 self-check questions: [notes]
prompts.notes.questions.detailed: Turn the notes into review questions: 5 on facts, 3 on understanding (“why”, “how is it connected”), 2 on application. Only ask about what's in the notes. Ask one at a time, wait for my answer and check it against the notes. Notes: [notes]
prompts.notes.questions.refine: Make the questions harder for the [section] section, where I made mistakes.
prompts.notes.questions.check: Based on my answers, which parts of the notes do I know worst?
prompts.notes.chapter.short: Make an outline of the chapter: [chapter text]
prompts.notes.chapter.detailed: Make a multi-level outline of the chapter: sections, sub-points, key concepts in each. One sentence per section saying what it's about. Don't retell in detail. Chapter text: [chapter text]
prompts.notes.chapter.refine: Mark which parts of the outline relate to the question [question].
prompts.notes.chapter.check: I've made my own outline: [outline]. What did I miss or put in the wrong place?
prompts.notes.compare.short: Compare two texts on the same topic: [text 1] and [text 2]
prompts.notes.compare.detailed: Compare two texts. Table: main idea, arguments, examples, conclusion, tone. Below the table: where they agree, where they differ, what appears in only one. Rely only on the texts. Text 1: [text 1]. Text 2: [text 2]
prompts.notes.compare.refine: Which text is more convincing on [question] and why? Point to specific passages.
prompts.notes.compare.check: My conclusion from the comparison: [conclusion]. Is it grounded in the texts?
prompts.notes.actions.short: Pull a to-do list out of my notes: [notes]
prompts.notes.actions.detailed: From the notes, list everything that needs doing. For each item: the action starting with a verb, who (if stated), deadline (if stated), where it came from. In a separate list, put things that look like tasks but it's unclear whether they were agreed. Don't invent names. Notes: [notes]
prompts.notes.actions.refine: Order the tasks by urgency and importance.
prompts.notes.actions.check: Which items are too vague to actually do?
prompts.notes.table.short: Turn this material into a table: [text]
prompts.notes.table.detailed: Turn the material into a table. Columns: [columns]. If the text has no data for a cell, write “not in text” rather than guessing. Below the table, one sentence on what it shows. Material: [text]
prompts.notes.table.refine: Suggest columns that would work better for comparing [items].
prompts.notes.table.check: Ask 5 questions that can only be answered from this table.
prompts.notes.verify.short: What in my notes should I double-check? [notes]
prompts.notes.verify.detailed: Read the notes and list everything worth double-checking: numbers, dates, names, quotes, unsourced claims, places where I might have misheard the lecturer. For each, why it's questionable and where to check it. Notes: [notes]
prompts.notes.verify.refine: Rank the items by risk: which would do the most damage if wrong.
prompts.notes.verify.check: I checked items [items] and found: [result]. Update the notes.
prompts.notes.cards.short: Make 15 question–answer cards from the material: [text]
prompts.notes.cards.detailed: Make spaced-repetition flashcards from the material. Rules: one fact per card, a short question, an answer of no more than 15 words, no ambiguity. Format: “Q: … / A: …”, one per line, so they're easy to import into a flashcard app. Material: [text]
prompts.notes.cards.refine: Card [number] is too complex. Split it into 2–3 simple ones.
prompts.notes.cards.check: Quiz me on the cards in random order and tell me at the end which to review.

verify.notes.summary: Compare the summary with the original: AI may leave out something important or add things that aren't in the text.
verify.notes.theses: Find every point in the original text. If you can't, the point was made up.
verify.notes.glossary: Definitions should match how terms are used in your material. General dictionary meanings may differ.
verify.notes.questions: Check answers against your own notes, not the AI's memory.
verify.notes.chapter: Compare the outline with the chapter's contents and subheadings.
verify.notes.compare: Make sure neither author is credited with the other's ideas: check against both texts.
verify.notes.actions: Check deadlines and owners: AI may treat a suggestion as a decision.
verify.notes.table: Check every cell against the source text, especially numbers and dates.
verify.notes.verify: This list is a prompt for checking, not the check itself. Verify each item against a reliable source.
verify.notes.cards: Cards should use your textbook's wording, not the AI's paraphrase.
